subject: The 'regime change' bomb that went off in their hands
alt: Alok's two-panel cartoon. In the top panel, two men in suits and ties run together on the left, tangled into each other, both pointing ahead with a finger. One of them carries a big black bomb with a lit fuse, marked in Devanagari: RIJEEM CHENJ (REGIME CHANGE). On the right, a bearded cleric in a black turban and a long grey robe stands with clenched fists, furious. In the bottom panel, a huge cloud of smoke and dust fills the left, with one hand sticking out of its edge; swirls and bright stars hang above. On the right the same cleric stands in the same place, now grinning with bared teeth. At the bottom left is the cartoonist's signature, ALOK, and at the bottom right the Sakal mark.
chutki: In the top panel two men in suits run together, fingers pointing at the turbaned figure ahead, a lit bomb in hand with the words: regime change. The man facing them has not moved; he just stands there, furious.

In the bottom panel the bomb has gone off, but it is the runners who have vanished into the cloud, one hand sticking out, with swirls and stars circling their heads. The man in the turban stands as before, and now he is grinning. Alok's joke is that the bomb picked up to change someone else's order went off in the hands that carried it. The target stands intact; those who played the gamble sit dizzy.
